0.0 s

b-tensor glyph

Superquadric glyph of B = R diag(λx, λy, λz) RT

Shape

Orientation

Rotation R = Rz(φ) Ry(θ) Rz(ψ), applied to the principal frame. Spin only matters for triaxial (non-axisymmetric) tensors.

Waveform

G(t) = a R K g(t): K scales the source axes (diagonal) and mixes them (off-diagonal), R rotates. The glyph shows the resulting b-tensor. Sweeps interpolate these parameters, so the waveform changes smoothly.

mT/m
Import waveforms
optional, same time unit

Paste one or more waveforms. Put a name on its own line before each one, or separate them with a blank line. A header line such as “gx gy gz t” is skipped. Evenly spaced times are read as samples with dt = Δt. Uneven times are read as the corner points of a piecewise-linear waveform and rasterized at 10 µs. An optional fifth column gives rf = ±1; without it the gradient is taken as the effective gradient, unless you enter a refocusing time. A single gradient column (g t) also works.

From MATLAB, with t an N × 1 vector: clipboard('copy', sprintf('%.9g %.9g %.9g %.9g\n', [gwf t]')). JSON from jsonencode(struct('name',…,'gwf',gwf,'t',t)) also works, optionally with 'rf', or with 'dt' instead of 't'; times in JSON are in s. A single gradient column is played on x.

View

Sweep and recording

    Transparency applies to images only. MP4 cannot store transparency, so videos always get the background shown in the view. For slides, choose White or Custom color under View to match the slide.

    Videos are H.264 MP4 files that open in PowerPoint. Record sweep renders frame by frame, so it never drops frames. Recordings capture exactly what the view shows, including slow rotation, caption and readout. Space plays the sweep, R toggles rotation.

    Glyph geometry follows Kindlmann's superquadric tensor glyphs (2004). Edge sharpness γ = 0 draws a plain ellipsoid. Invariants use the Haeberlen convention: bΔ ∈ [−½, 1], bη ∈ [0, 1]. Triaxiality τ = 4bΔ²bη², the triaxial part of the normalized eigenvalue variance bΔ²(1 + bη²/3), scaled to reach 1 at eigenvalues b(0, ⅓, ⅔). It is 0 for axisymmetric and isotropic tensors.
